options.title: Why does anyone live on Tristan da Cunha?
options.first_line: Why does anyone live on Tristan da Cunha, a lone volcano in the middle of the South Atlantic?
options.first_frame: The South Atlantic on the old map, a tiny volcano island at its centre with its name writing on and a pin pulsing, waves rolling all round it and no other land in sight.

options.title: Tristan da Cunha has no airport. Why live there?
options.first_line: Tristan da Cunha has no airport and no neighbours. So why do people live there?
options.first_frame: A tiny island on an empty ocean map, a crossed-out airplane sign stamped beside it and a fishing boat bobbing at its shore.

options.title: Who would settle Tristan da Cunha?
options.first_line: Tristan da Cunha is the most remote island anyone lives on. Who chose to settle here?
options.first_frame: The camera already diving from the whole globe down onto a single dot in the South Atlantic, the name TRISTAN DA CUNHA landing on it.

why: Calling it the most remote inhabited island tells a stranger why this dot matters, and 'who chose to settle here?' is a question they have to stay for; the globe-to-dot dive also shows the remoteness with the sound off.
